relationships.subject: cation-chloride cotransporter dysregulation
relationships.evidence_quote: dysregulation of CCCs has emerged as a key mechanism underlying neurological disorders including epilepsy, neuropathic pain, and autism spectrum disorder

key_findings: The strength of GABA/glycine-mediated inhibition depends on the neuronal Cl- gradient, which is set primarily by the cation-chloride cotransporters NKCC1 and KCC2.
Dysregulation of CCCs, regulated by activity and protein interactions, is a key mechanism in epilepsy, neuropathic pain and autism spectrum disorder (review).
